pages.title: Home - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Ed Willkie Middle School (EWMS) is a campus of Eagle Mountain-Saginaw Independent School District (EMS ISD). Tagline on the home page: "We Are EMS Proud."

Contact Info (site footer): 6129 Texas Shiner Road, Fort Worth, TX 76179. Phone: 817-237-9631. Fax: 817-847-2970. The campus displays the Purple Star campus designation logo.

District mission (shown on the EWMS home page): "The mission of Eagle Mountain-Saginaw Independent School District is to foster a culture of excellence that instills a passion for a lifetime of continuous achievement in every student."

Why EMS ISD / What Makes Us Different:
- World Class Educators: EMS ISD is home to world-class educators who are dedicated, highly skilled, and committed to inspiring and empowering students for success.
- Personalized Opportunities: EMS ISD offers personalized opportunities through diverse academic programs, extracurricular activities, and tailored support to help each student reach their full potential.
- Family Culture: The family culture at EMS ISD is built on strong relationships, collaboration, and a supportive community that prioritizes student success and well-being.

A Culture of Excellence: "We believe that every student deserves to learn something new every day. We strive to prepare young people to succeed in high-demand occupations in today's competitive global economy."

Upcoming events listed on the home page (fall 2026): MS Choir Region Clinic & Concert (Nov 7, 2026); EWMS Beginner Band Concert (Nov 10, 2026, 6:00-7:00 PM, Ed Willkie MS Competition Gym, enter through door #20); TMEA MS Region Band Clinic/Concert (Dec 4-5, 2026, Cleburne High School).

The school's Facebook feed references students who "worked the Willkie Way" during the first six weeks by passing all their classes and following the student code of conduct, and a "Badger Bleacher Bunch" spirit group at pep rallies.

pages.title: About Us - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Who We Are: Ed Willkie Middle School, home of the Badgers, is a proud and spirited campus in Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD. We serve students in grades 6-8 from the southwest portion of the district. Known for strong academics, meaningful relationships, and a focus on the whole child, Ed Willkie is a place where students are supported, challenged, and empowered to grow.

Mission: "The mission of Ed Willkie Middle School is to cultivate relationships, empower students, and foster growth in a safe and supportive environment that promotes lifelong learning and success."

Motto: "Every student. Unique. Limitless."

The Willkie Way: At Ed Willkie, we "Work the Willkie Way" by upholding a culture grounded in being Exceptional, Wise, Mindful, and Safe.

We celebrate students through programs like Perfect Attendance, Honor Roll, and Student of the Month, and we recognize staff through student-nominated awards and team-building events.

Highlights of our campus culture include:
- Strong academic programs that prepare students for high school and beyond
- Opportunities to excel in athletics, fine arts, academic competitions, and leadership organizations
- A supportive environment focused on recognition, connection, and future readiness

History: Ed Willkie Middle School opened in 2008 and was named in honor of Mr. Ed Willkie (1933-2020), a lifelong educator and dedicated EMS ISD Board of Education member. Mr. Willkie served on the board for 30 years, becoming a voice for public education and a champion for students, teachers, and families. His legacy of leadership continues to shape the values and vision of the school that bears his name.

Feeder campuses: Ed Willkie Middle School serves students who reside in the southwest portion of Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD. Our feeder campuses include Dozier Elementary, Greenfield Elementary, and Chisholm Trail High School. Together, we empower students to grow as learners, leaders, and members of the Badger community.

pages.title: Campus Namesake - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Mr. Ed Willkie joined Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD as a Board Member and served more than 30 years in various capacities. He felt like he did not get the best quality education as a child and wanted to make a difference. He believed all students should get equal opportunity. He was a proud supporter of EMS ISD and always believed it is a shining star in the great state of Texas.

Mr. Willkie was born on May 30, 1933, in a little farmhouse on the outskirts of Zionsville, Indiana, during the Great Depression. In 1946, his family moved to Wisconsin, where Mr. Willkie attended school. He was an athlete who played basketball and football and was state recognized in both sports. His basketball team was #1 in the state for 14 consecutive weeks, and his scoring record stood for 62 years.

He attended Stout University, which is part of the University of Wisconsin, Home of the Badgers. This is where the Ed Willkie Middle School mascot gets its roots. Mr. Willkie was unable to finish college; however, he worked his way up in a magazine company to become one of the youngest Vice Presidents of a company. In 1969, he and his wife moved to Fort Worth, where he worked in the manufacturing industry and then owned a candy display business until his retirement.

He served on the EMS ISD Board of Education for 30 years, serving 12 of those as Board President. He was instrumental in the strategic growth of the district as it expanded from five campuses to 23 during his Board tenure.

Mr. Willkie and his wife, Madonna, celebrated more than 60 years of marriage and raised three children, who all attended EMS ISD schools.

Mr. Willkie passed away on Thursday, January 30, 2020. His legacy of service and advocacy for EMS ISD and public education lives on in his challenge to the Willkie Badgers to "keep on doing a great job!" The Badger Family is truly grateful for the lasting impact that Mr. Ed Willkie made to our community, our campus, and EMS ISD.

pages.title: Campus Procedures - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Visiting Our Campus: To ensure the safety and security of everyone, all visitors, including parents and guardians, are required to check in at the front office upon arrival. Once signed in, a visitor badge will be provided and should be worn at all times while on school grounds. On state assessment days, the campus is closed to visitors.

Arrival Procedures:
- Doors open at 8:30 a.m. for student entry.
- Breakfast is served from 8:30-9:00 a.m. Students must be in line by 8:45 a.m. to be served.
- All personal devices (phones, tablets, earbuds, headphones, etc.) must be turned off and put away for the entirety of the school day, 8:30 a.m.-4:22 p.m. Violations of the device policy may require parent pickup and a fee to retrieve the device.

Dismissal Procedures:
- Early pick-up ends at 4:02 p.m. After this time, students will not be released until the regular dismissal at 4:22 p.m.
- Students are expected to leave campus promptly at dismissal unless participating in a supervised school activity.
- Students not picked up within 15 minutes of school or activity dismissal may lose certain privileges due to limited supervision.

Student ID Requirement: All students are required to wear an Ed Willkie student ID on a school-approved lanyard. The first ID and lanyard are provided free of charge. Replacement IDs can be obtained by following campus replacement procedures.

Attendance: Regular attendance helps students grow academically and socially. Full details are in the Student and Parent Handbook.

Tardies: Arriving to class on time is an important part of supporting a positive learning environment. Each campus has its own tardy procedures; contact the school office with questions.

Enrollment: Visit the EMS ISD Registration page for required documents, how-to videos, an attendance zone finder, and step-by-step guidance. Withdrawing: notify the campus at least three school days before the student's last day; contact the campus registrar. Transfers: see the EMS ISD Transfer Policy.

The page also links to the Dress Code and the Student & Parent Handbook & Code of Conduct.

pages.title: Academics - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
At Ed Willkie Middle School, academic excellence is the foundation of everything we do. Through a diverse and rigorous curriculum, we provide students with the knowledge, skills, and personalized learning experiences they need to thrive, both now and in the future.

Our instructional programs are built on the belief that:
- Every student is a unique individual with the ability to achieve success
- Engaged learners grow deeper in understanding and confidence
- High expectations paired with strong support lead to lifelong achievement

We are proud to offer rich and varied learning experiences that equip students for success at graduation and beyond.

Quote featured on the page: "What lies behind us and what lies before us are tiny matters compared to what lies within us." - Ralph Waldo Emerson

Academics navigation also links to: English Language Arts & Reading, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, Accountability, Career and Technology Education, College, Career, and Military Readiness, and Advanced Academics (district pages).

pages.title: English Language Arts & Reading - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
The primary goal of Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD's Secondary English Language Arts and Reading courses is for all students to graduate as confident, analytical readers, proficient, reflective writers, effective communicators, and discerning consumers of visual media.

Secondary literacy instruction is grounded in the RLA RBIS (Research-Based Instructional Strategies) Framework:
- the systematic and explicit teaching of foundational skills
- knowledge-building instruction
- Tier-1, TEKS-aligned instruction and practice centered on grade-level or above, complex texts
- oral and written responses to text

Students read and respond to increasingly complex texts across a variety of literary, informational, and argumentative genres. Daily academic discussions and collaboration with peers deepens students' understanding of themselves, the community, and the world around them. Engaging in the writing process, students write for specific purposes and audiences, emphasizing clarity, diction, coherence, organization, and adherence to conventions.

Instructional Materials: Middle School ELAR uses McGraw-Hill StudySync. (High School English uses HMH Into Literature.) More district-level curriculum information is on the EMS ISD Curriculum & Instruction page.

pages.title: Mathematics - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
At EMS ISD, we are dedicated to fostering a culture of excellence that supports a lifetime of continuous achievement for every student. Our mathematics department is committed to nurturing critical thinkers who embrace the journey of learning and the process of problem-solving.

We believe in the power of productive struggle, where students are encouraged to persevere through challenges, developing resilience and a deeper understanding of mathematical concepts. Our approach emphasizes the importance of the process over the final answer, guiding students to explore, question, and connect ideas.

Join us as we inspire a passion for mathematics and equip our students with the skills and mindset needed for success in an ever-changing world.

Instructional Materials (Middle School):
- Bluebonnet Mathematics: 6th, 7th, and 8th Grade Math
- Carnegie Learning: 6th and 7th Grade Advanced Math

(High School: SAVVAS for Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2; Cosenza & Associates for Algebraic Reasoning; Cengage for Precalculus, Calculus AB, Calculus BC; MacMillan for AP Statistics.)

pages.title: Science - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD scientists make connections across disciplines to build a framework of understanding through recurring themes and concepts. They learn to integrate science and engineering practices, such as asking questions, developing models, analyzing data, and constructing explanations. By investigating real-world phenomena, students deepen their insights and apply their knowledge to design innovative solutions to complex problems.

Students analyze and interpret data to understand meaning, identify features and patterns, and uncover relationships or correlations. This approach helps them develop evidence-based arguments, evaluate designs, and effectively communicate their findings.

Vision: To be at the forefront of science education.
Mission: To create a community of lifelong learners who are globally competitive citizens.

The goal of EMS ISD science is to foster a culture of inquiry where all learners are challenged by a curriculum rich in discovery, scientific and engineering processes, and experimental design.

Instructional Materials: Savvas; Accelerate Learning STEMScopes; Rice University OpenStax; Texas Parks and Wildlife.

pages.title: Social Studies - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD's social studies program provides a comprehensive exploration of our world and its history. Sixth grade students examine contemporary world cultures, followed by an in-depth study of Texas history in seventh grade and U.S. history in eighth grade. High school students have access to a wide range of courses, including World Geography, World History, U.S. History, Government, and Economics, as well as a diverse selection of electives and Advanced Placement opportunities for advanced learners.

Instructional Materials: Discovery Education; McGraw Hill; The DBQ Project.

pages.title: Extracurriculars - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
At Ed Willkie Middle School, learning doesn't stop when the school day ends. Our extracurricular programs provide students with meaningful ways to explore interests, build relationships, and grow as confident, capable leaders.

Through a wide range of opportunities, including athletics, fine arts, and student-led clubs, students are encouraged to:
- Find their voice and express their creativity
- Develop leadership skills through teamwork, service, and competition
- Build lasting connections with peers and mentors

Whether on the field, on stage, or serving in the community, these experiences shape students who are not only active learners but inspired contributors ready to lead and succeed beyond high school.

Extracurricular areas: Athletics, Fine Arts (Band, Choir, Theatre, Visual Arts), and Clubs and Organizations.

pages.title: Athletics - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
At EMS ISD, athletics is more than just competition; it's a gateway to growth, teamwork, and life lessons. Our programs offer students the opportunity to challenge themselves, develop leadership skills, and be part of something bigger.

Athletics mission: to prepare student-athletes to be highly successful in the classroom, community, and on the athletic fields, so they understand and embrace the honor and respect they need to achieve athletically and academically at the next level. The staff is committed to teaching life lessons through athletics and promoting team unity.

Sports offered at Ed Willkie (per site navigation): 6th Grade Pre-Athletics, Basketball (Boys and Girls), Cheer, Cross Country, Football, Golf, Gymnastics, Soccer (Boys and Girls), Tennis, Track & Field, Volleyball, and EMS Trailblazers Special Olympics. Schedules are posted on Rank One.

Physicals: Your child must have a physical to be in the athletics class and participate in a sport. Physicals must be dated after May 1 for the upcoming school year. All athletes must have a physical, medical history, and complete the required online forms each year through Rank One.

Athletic Uniforms: Students must purchase an athletic uniform (1 shirt and 1 pair of shorts) for $35.00 through RevTrak. Additional sets are optional.

Participation: In middle school, students are encouraged to participate in as many sports as possible. Most sports require a tryout; the exception is football, where there are no cuts. Students who participate in football, volleyball, or basketball must be enrolled in the athletics class.
- Cross Country and Track take place before or after school, so the athletics class is not required (but recommended).
- Soccer and Tennis each have their own athletic period.
- Golf and Gymnastics take place off campus at the feeder high schools, led by EMS ISD high school coaches. Parents transport students to the high school; a bus returns students to the middle school. Golfers must bring their own clubs.

A middle school athletic trainer handles healthcare administration, education, and the prevention, evaluation, treatment, and rehabilitation of injuries. The page links to a Middle School Athletics Handbook and the EMS ISD Athletics Department.

pages.title: Clubs and Organizations - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Get connected, try something new, and make lasting memories. There's something for everyone; your journey starts here! Check the EWMS Student Hub in Canvas for more information and meeting times. Parents can sign up for a Canvas Parent Observer Account to view club information, meeting details, and more.

Clubs and organizations at Ed Willkie Middle School:
- Academic UIL
- Academic Quiz Team (6th, 7th, and 8th grade teams)
- PATHS
- National Junior Honor Society
- Student Council
- Yearbook
- Pokemon Club
- Fellowship of Christian Athletes

"We're saving a spot for you!"

pages.title: Fine Arts - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
IMAGINE. CREATE. PERFORM.

At EWMS, we believe fine arts are a vital part of a well-rounded educational experience. Our students have the opportunity to explore and grow through a wide range of artistic programs that inspire creativity, discipline, collaboration, and self-expression. Whether your passion is in band, dance, theatre, or visual arts, you'll find a place to shine and belong in our vibrant fine arts community. Badger artists are making their mark both on campus and beyond.

EMS ISD Fine Arts Department Mission Statement: The mission of EMS ISD Fine Arts is to equip every student with the skills, confidence, and creativity to thrive in performance and beyond while fostering artistic growth, academic excellence, and real-world readiness through dynamic fine arts experiences.

Ed Willkie Fine Arts Programs: Band, Choir, Theatre, and Visual Arts. Each program offers students the chance to explore their passions, build new skills, and connect with others through creativity and performance. From the first brushstroke to the final bow, each program provides meaningful experiences that shape confident, well-rounded individuals. A Fine Arts Calendar is available on the site.

pages.title: Band - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
The Sound of Tradition. Experience the Sound.

The Ed Willkie MS Band has earned numerous excellent and superior ratings, a reflection of the dedication, talent, and hard work of our students and directors.

More than a music program, the Ed Willkie Band is a place where students grow as musicians, build lasting friendships, and take pride in their achievements. We're excited to share our tradition of excellence and invite you to be part of the band experience.

The band staff includes a Band Director, a Band Assistant Director, and a Percussion Specialist. Band registration forms are completed through Rank One. To stay connected, follow Ed Willkie Band on Facebook (facebook.com/willkieband). Students can visit the EWMS Canvas Course and parents can create a Canvas Parent Observer account for class-specific updates.

A Beginner Band Concert is scheduled for Nov 10, 2026 in the Ed Willkie MS Competition Gym.

pages.title: Choir - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Inspiring Voices. Ed Willkie Chorale is dedicated to developing a lifelong understanding and appreciation of music in every student.

Through engaging instruction and meaningful performance experiences, students build the skills, knowledge, and confidence to succeed both in music and throughout their academic journey. More than just a class, our choir program is a place where students grow as individuals, connect through shared creativity, and find joy in making music together.

The mission of the Ed Willkie Chorale is to cultivate students who are recognized throughout our campus for their character, leadership, and sense of responsibility through the study and performance of music.

Motto: "SING TOGETHER. ACHIEVE TOGETHER!"

The choir is led by a Choir Director. Follow the choir on Instagram (@ewms_choir). Students can visit the EWMS Canvas Course and parents can create a Canvas Parent Observer account for updates.

pages.title: Theatre - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
"Theatre is more than just a stage we're going through!"

Welcome to Ed Willkie Middle School Theatre! We welcome all students, whether you're a seasoned performer or just stepping into the spotlight, enrolled in a theatre class or joining from the sidelines.

Our program is open to anyone with a passion for creativity, self-expression, and storytelling. At Willkie, every student has the chance to explore the world of theatre, grow in confidence, and let their talent shine, on stage and beyond.

Come as you are, and bring the drama; we'll help you take it from there!

The program is led by a Theatre Arts Director.

pages.title: Visual Arts - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
The Art of Expression. The Ed Willkie art program provides middle school students the opportunity to be creative and artistic while using a wide variety of mediums.

Open to students in grades 6, 7, and 8, Visual Arts at Ed Willkie encourages imagination, self-expression, and skill-building through hands-on projects. In a supportive and engaging environment, students explore their creativity while developing confidence in their artistic abilities.
- Students work with a range of materials and techniques
- Projects are designed to inspire originality and creative thinking
- Artwork is often displayed in school and district-wide exhibitions

We invite students to discover the joy of creating and to express their unique voice, one project at a time.

Quote featured on the page: "You can't use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have." - Maya Angelou

The program is led by an Art Teacher and links to the Visual Arts Scholastic Events (VASE) program.

pages.title: For Families - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
At Ed Willkie Middle School, families are essential partners in our mission to foster a culture of excellence and lifelong learning for every student. This section is your one-stop resource for staying connected, informed, and engaged.

We're committed to supporting you with:
- Helpful tools and up-to-date information
- Ongoing communication to strengthen the home-school connection
- A welcoming environment where your role in your student's success is valued

Together, we empower every student to grow with purpose, achieve with confidence, and succeed for life.

For Families navigation links: Family Quick Links, Campus Calendar, Military Families, Safety and Security, and Let's Get Social.

pages.title: Military Families - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD is proud to welcome and support military-connected students and their families. With close proximity to NAS JRB Fort Worth, we recognize the unique challenges and opportunities that come with military life. Our district is committed to providing a welcoming environment, academic continuity, and personalized support from enrollment to graduation. We honor your service and are here to serve you.

EMS ISD supports military-connected families through:
- A designated Military Family Liaison at every campus
- Personalized academic planning support for smooth course transitions
- Access to counseling and social-emotional services tailored to mobile students
- Annual recognitions such as Veterans Day and Month of the Military Child
- Enrollment and withdrawal processes designed to align with military timelines
- Partnerships with NAS JRB Fort Worth and military-connected organizations
- Children of an active duty member of the armed forces, mobilized reservist, or member of the Texas National Guard qualify for Pre-K.

Each EMS ISD campus has one Military Family Liaison who serves as the primary contact for transitioning military-connected students and families. Responsibilities include supporting enrollment, course planning, and student transitions; connecting families with academic and social-emotional resources; communicating proactively with staff and families; coordinating campus-based military recognitions; and promoting a positive, welcoming environment. Ed Willkie's campus military contacts can be reached through the main office at 817-237-9631.

FAQ highlights: When a child enrolls at a new EMS ISD campus, the campus liaison connects with the family to support enrollment and transition. All campuses offer tutoring and counseling support; military-connected students may also access 24/7 support through Tutor.com. Campuses participate in Month of the Military Child, Purple Up! Days, Veterans Day assemblies, and other recognitions.

Resources linked: Pre-K & Kinder Registration, Enrollment & Registration, District Maps & Attendance Zones, School Calendars, School Menus, Military Interstate Compact (MIC3), Military Child Education Coalition, Military OneSource, and a TEA/MCEC video series on supporting military-connected students.

pages.title: Library - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Welcome to the Ed Willkie Library. Our library is a vibrant hub for discovery, collaboration, and learning. Whether you're researching, reading for pleasure, or working on a group project, the library is here to help you grow, explore, and succeed. A Library Search (Follett catalog) is available online.

The library is staffed by a Librarian.

The EMS ISD library team will create inviting environments with state-of-the-art resources, facilities, and equipment where students, staff, and community members are actively engaged in collaborative learning endeavors.

As an integral part of the Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD learning community, the library and media services program provides guidance, resources, and collaborative instruction for students and staff to gain the skills necessary to become effective, life-long learners and ethical and creative users of ideas and information.

pages.title: PTO - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
When families, schools, and communities work together, students thrive. At Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD, we believe that meaningful partnerships create powerful learning experiences. From volunteering in classrooms to participating in parent organizations, there are many ways to contribute to the success of our students and schools.

Visitors vs. Volunteers: A visitor is a person allowed to attend campus functions and/or lunch with their child; no volunteer form is needed, just check in with your driver's license in the front office. Volunteers are given an assignment or task dealing directly with children other than their own while on campus or on school-sponsored trips. Volunteers must complete the Volunteer Application and have an annual criminal history check completed by the District on file. The background check must be completed and approved before volunteering. Volunteers are processed through the district's Raptor visitor system, which scans your driver's license each time you come to campus. All volunteers are required to reapply each year.

Apply to Be a Volunteer: Complete the Volunteer Application and Criminal History Information (English or Spanish application through Raptor). It can take up to 14 days for applications to process. Only one application is necessary per school year. Questions about the volunteer process go to the front office of your child's school.

Parent organizations: The district's most active groups are the Parent-Teacher Associations (PTA) at each elementary campus and the Parent Teacher Organization (PTO) at each middle and high school campus, including Ed Willkie Middle School. These groups help raise funds for worthwhile projects and serve the schools and their students in a number of ways. The EMS ISD PTO is on Facebook (PTOEMSISD). Ed Willkie's PTO has campus roles for Hospitality, Membership, Volunteer Coordinator, and Community Service; contact the school office for details on how to join.

pages.title: Counselor's Corner - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Here for you, every step of the way. Support You Can Count On.

Our Counseling Department is committed to supporting the academic, personal, and social growth of every student. Our counselors partner with students, families, and staff to help create a supportive and engaging middle school experience where every student feels encouraged, prepared, and confident as they grow.

Whether you have questions about classes, need help navigating challenges, or are looking for guidance during the transition to high school, we're here to support you.

The counseling team includes two School Counselors (assigned by student last name: A-L and M-Z) and an Intervention Counselor. Students can join the counseling Canvas course.

Counseling resource links: District Counseling Page, Academic Planning, How to Get Support, Personal & Social Development, Resources, SchooLinks, and Safety & Prevention.

Campus Registrar: Our campus registrar manages student records and supports enrollment and withdrawal processes in alignment with district and state guidelines. While much of the enrollment process is completed online, the registrar is available to assist with questions and ensure all required documentation is accurate and complete. For questions about enrolling, withdrawing, or updating records, contact the campus registrar through the main office.

pages.title: Administration - Ed Willkie Middle School
pages.content:
Meet Our Campus Leaders.

- Dan Russell, Principal
- Sara Carrillo, Assistant Principal (student last names A-L)
- Kristie Ryan, Assistant Principal (student last names M-Z)

Our campus administrators are dedicated to supporting students, families, and staff every day. As leaders in learning, they are here to serve, guide, and partner with you to ensure a positive, safe, and successful school experience for every student.

At EMS ISD, we believe education is a team effort. Our leadership teams work collaboratively to foster a culture of excellence and continuous achievement for every student.

Administrators can be reached through the main office at 817-237-9631 or via the Let's Talk system.
